findings.title: Cycles made only of arrays are not detected (RangeError / cycles option ignored)
findings.property: A circular structure either throws TypeError('Converting circular structure to JSON') or, with opts.cycles true, yields '__cycle__' in place of the cycle
findings.property_test: circular array throws TypeError or yields __cycle__
findings.input: const a = []; a.push(a); index(a) and index(a, {cycles:true})
findings.actual: RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded in both cases
findings.evidence: README documents the cycles option (cycle detection returns '__cycle__', otherwise TypeError as in JSON.stringify). Code only records objects in `seen` after the Array.isArray branch returns, so arrays are never tracked.

review.title: Cycles consisting only of arrays are not detected and cause a RangeError (stack overflow)
review.reason: index.js returns from the Array.isArray branch (lines 29-36) before `seen` is checked or updated (lines 40-45), so an array that contains itself recurses until the stack overflows. Cycles that pass through an object are detected, either throwing TypeError or returning '__cycle__' when `opts.cycles` is true. The README documents `cycles`, and the library mirrors JSON.stringify, which throws TypeError for this input, so the pure-array case is inconsistent and ignores `cycles`. The README wording ('circular property') and the exact expected output '["__cycle__"]' are the reporter's extrapolation, and it is an edge case that throws either way, which is why severity is low. A small fix (track arrays in `seen`) would be accepted.

fix.reason: the repro passes on the patched code
